Subject: Capacity plan comparison — Dedicated reservation vs Private (analysis + recommendation)

Seth / team —

Attached is a concise capacity matrix (redwood_capacity_matrix_v3.xlsx) and the executive summary below. I modeled three workload tiers from the CSV you provided: baseline (avg 45 QPS), peak (220 QPS sustained during working hours), and burst (peaks to ~900 concurrent tokens for scheduled batch windows). I included A100-80GB equivalents as our baseline GPU unit for parity.

Executive summary (short):
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved capacity): lower time-to-live (fastest onboarding), predictable per-token economics, and minimal ops burden for MedSys. For your SLOs (p95 <220ms for 512-token), estimated steady-state for peak load: 8 x A100-80GB equivalents with continuous batching + KV cache, with autoscale headroom to 12 for burst windows. 30-day pilot recommendation: reserve 8 GPUs (dedicated pool), 10% burst credit, keys in customer-managed KMS (we support an encrypted tunnel).

- Private (VPC or on-prem): higher initial capex/commitment and longer lead time due to networking and procurement (2–8 weeks for VPC onboarding; 6–12 weeks for air-gapped on-prem). For equivalent tail latency under your retention/SLA constraints, the Private footprint is ~12 x A100-80GB equivalents to allow for OS/hypervisor overhead, on-prem storage for retention, and redundant capacity for maintenance windows. Operational overhead includes customer IT for rack/networking + Redwood private agent install and quarterly security attestations.

Cost and operational tradeoffs (high level):
- Latency: both meet p95 target when right-sized; Dedicated has faster autoscaling and better burst smoothing because we control the orchestration layer.
- Cost: Dedicated shows ~20–30% lower upfront spend for year 1 at your forecast volumes because of shared-managed optimizations (batching, cross-customer cache savings) and Redwood Optimize recommendations. Private becomes cost-competitive after ~18–24 months if you fully amortize hardware and ops.
- Compliance: Private offers the strongest isolation and easier evidence for air-gapped audit requirements. Dedicated can meet SOC2 / customer KMS needs in VPC configurations and we provide audit logs for the 90-day retention you specified.

Recommendation: run a 30–60 day pilot on Dedicated reserved capacity (8 GPUs) with a scoped set of production traffic routed through a dedicated pool + customer-managed KMS. Parallel: begin procurement and network prep for Private if you have a hard mandate for air-gapped deployments. This hedges time-to-market vs isolation requirements.

Proposed mutual action plan (MAP):
1) Agree scope & success metrics (latency p95, daily error rate, cost per 1k tokens) — target by Fri 7/17.
2) Redwood sets up Dedicated reserved pool (8x A100-80GB equivalents) and provides SST+KMS integration docs — deliver in 5 business days after contract.
3) MedSys provides test keys and a 7-day rolling sample traffic stream from your staging environment.
4) Joint review at day 14 with metrics dashboard and quality checks; decide go/no-go for Private procurement.

I've attached the capacity matrix and a one-page cost delta. Note: numbers assume quantized model footprint (int8) for cost estimates; we can run exact benchmarks if you want a model-by-model comparison.
